God, if He wants to do something, what would hinder it, and who would resist Him? For what the holy God wants, who would scatter? And whose hand would turn back the high hand? Therefore, to show that God is by nature and truly, it would be said reasonably by Him, 'All my counsel will stand, and all that I have purposed, I will do.' Then He says, 'I will call a bird from the east, and from a far-off land, concerning what I have purposed.' And it follows, 'I am.' The bird called from the east and from a far-off land, we say, is the Babylonian, who burned the whole land of the Jews, took Jerusalem, and destroyed the temple. Then, having raised many of the common people and prominent ones, he led them away, and having taken them, he imposed a harsh and unbearable yoke of captivity on them. And it will be clear to you from what God said to the blessed prophet Ezekiel.

The great eagle with long wings, full of claws, which has the story of entering Lebanon, took the choice parts of the cedar, the topmost tender shoots, and brought them to the land of Canaan, to a fortified city, and took from the seed of the land, and gave it to the plain as a plant, in much water, and set it under care, and it became a weak vine, and small in size, and its branches were on it, and its roots were under the ground. And it became a vine and produced fruit, and spread out its branches. God spoke to the prophet Ezekiel. Since the word was hard to understand, and the power of the thoughts was not very clear to the listeners, he himself interprets it again, saying: I spoke to the rebellious house of Israel, you do not know what these things are that I said. When the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, and takes its king and leaders, and brings them to Babylon. And he will take from the seed of the kingdom, and make a covenant with him, and bring him into an oath, and take the leaders of the land to make a weak kingdom, and not to exalt themselves to keep his covenant, and establish it.
pass_b_english: If God desires to act, what could possibly hinder Him, and who could stand to resist Him? For who would dare to scatter that which the holy God intends? And whose hand could ever turn back His high hand? Therefore, to demonstrate that God is truly and by nature so, it is reasonably said of Him, 'All my counsel will stand, and all that I have purposed, I will do' (Isaiah 46:10). Then He declares, 'I will call a bird from the east, and from a far-off land, concerning what I have purposed' (Isaiah 46:11). And the consequence follows, 'I am.'

This bird, called from the east and from a far-off land, is the Babylonian, who laid waste to the whole land of the Jews, seized Jerusalem, and destroyed the temple. Having raised up many among both the common people and the prominent, he led them away, and once he had taken them, he imposed upon them a harsh and unbearable yoke of captivity. This will become clear to you through what God spoke to the blessed prophet Ezekiel.

The great eagle with long wings of great extension and full of claws, whose narrative involves entering Lebanon, took the choice parts of the cedar, the topmost tender shoots, and brought them to the land of Canaan to a fortified city; he took from the seed of the land and planted it in the plain amidst much water, setting it under care, until it became a weak vine, small in size, with its branches upon it and its roots beneath the ground. It became a vine that produced fruit and spread out its branches. God spoke these things to the prophet Ezekiel.

Because the word was difficult to understand and the power of the thoughts was not very clear to those listening, he himself interprets it once more, saying: 'I spoke to the rebellious house of Israel, yet you do not know what these things are that I have said.' When the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem, he takes its king and its leaders and brings them to Babylon.

He will take from the seed of the kingdom, making a covenant with him and bringing him into an oath, and he will take the leaders of the land to establish a weak kingdom, so that they shall not exalt themselves to keep his covenant and establish it.
